key_insight: AdaEvolve introduces an adaptive controller for LLM-driven evolutionary program search that dynamically reallocates inference budget based on non-stationary search dynamics, cutting wasted compute on stagnating populations while focusing effort on promising candidates.
problem_solved: Static schedules for using LLMs as semantic mutation operators in inference-time evolutionary search waste compute because they cannot respond to changing search progress or population stagnation.
method: Frame LLM-driven program generation as a zeroth-order optimization loop where an LLM proposes mutations and a fitness evaluator ranks candidates.
Monitor search dynamics (e.g., improvement rate, diversity, stagnation) and use an adaptive controller to reallocate inference budget, mutation intensity, or selection pressure in real time.
Prioritize promising subpopulations and throttle or suspend effort on stagnating ones to improve sample-efficiency and reduce wasted LLM queries.
impact: Makes inference-time LLM search far more compute-efficient and practical for automated program synthesis and similar tasks, enabling higher-quality results for the same or lower inference cost.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: evolutionary loop with LLM mutation, fitness evaluation, selection and an adaptive controller that adjusts budget arrows.
Before vs after bar/stacked chart: compute spent on promising vs stagnating populations comparing static vs adaptive schedules.
Timeline/heatmap: search progress over time showing faster improvement and fewer wasted queries under AdaEvolve.
Icon set: LLM (brain), budget meter (coin/clock), mutation operator (DNA/gear), and fitness gauge (speedometer)
paper_title: AdaEvolve: Adaptive LLM Driven Zeroth-Order Optimization
paper_authors: Mert Cemri, Shubham Agrawal, Akshat Gupta, Shu Liu, Audrey Cheng
